 Log in Rookie of the Year announcement kicks off Awards Week (LIVE on MLB Network, MLB+)
 27 minutes ago MLB.com
 Share share-square--:R1qlq: Of all the annual Baseball Writers' Association of America Awards, each league's Rookie of the Year honor gives us the best glimpse into the future of the game. Many Rookies of the Year past have gone on to multiple All-Star selections and even Hall of Fame careers.
 Full coverage of Awards season 
 What's in store for this year's winner in each league? Well, first we need to find out who the winners are, and the announcement is being made right now on MLB Network and MLB+.
 All-time Rookie of the Year Award winners 
 AL winner 
 Kevin McGonigle , INF, Tigers 
 McGonigle is the sixth Tiger to earn Rookie of the Year honors and the first Detroit position player to win it since Lou Whitaker in 1978. Entering the season as the No. 2 overall prospect in MLB, McGonigle more than lived up to the hype as he led the American League with 7.1 WAR , according to Baseball-Reference.
 Just 21 years old for most of the season, McGonigle displayed plate discipline far beyond his years. He rarely chased out of the zone and had a walk rate (13.4%) that nearly equaled his strikeout rate (14.1%). That heavily contributed to the lefty hitter’s .376 on-base percentage, which paced all qualified rookies and ranked sixth in the AL.
 McGonigle also scored 97 runs, the eighth-most in the AL, while batting at or near the top of Detroit’s lineup. McGonigle is the fifth rookie in AL/NL history to post at least 95 walks and 95 runs scored since the Rookie of the Year Award was established in 1947, joining Aaron Judge (2017), Hall of Famer Joe Morgan (1965), Jim Gilliam (1953) and Al Rosen (1950).
 McGonigle, who was selected to the AL All-Star team, also provided decent pop (18 home runs) and speed (12 stolen bases) while playing more than 90 games each at shortstop and third base. That versatility, blended with his plus skills at the plate, is why he was voted as the junior circuit’s top rookie.
 Plus, as a result of McGonigle’s win, the Tigers earn a supplemental first-round Draft pick next year under the Prospect Promotion Incentive , an extra reward for the club’s decision to add its top prospect to its Opening Day roster out of Spring Training.
 NL finalists 
 Carson Benge , OF, Mets 
 The top tool for Benge is his arm, which allowed him to lead the NL with 10 outfield assists as a right fielder. But Benge excelled in other areas, too. If you throw out the first 30 games of his career, he finished with a .302/.366/.462 slash line, along with 20 doubles, 18 homers and 16 stolen bases in 126 games. Of the four Major Leaguers to bat higher than .302 over that same stretch, only Yordan Alvarez finished with more than 18 homers. And Alvarez is decidedly not a rookie.
 Sal Stewart , INF, Reds 
 After a one-month cameo in 2025, Stewart opened 2026 in the big leagues and his spot in manager Terry Francona's lineup -- fourth -- provided indication of how confident the Reds were in his abilities. The 22-year-old first baseman batted .263 with a .787 OPS, 32 home runs and 112 RBIs. 
 Stewart became the first Reds rookie -- and the 15th rookie overall -- to produce a 30-homer/100-RBI season. Each of the previous nine players that did it since the Rookie of the Year Award began (1947) won it. That list includes superstars Pete Alonso (2019), Aaron Judge (2017) and Albert Pujols (2001).
 JJ Wetherholt , 2B, Cardinals 
 No NL rookie produced a higher fWAR than Wetherholt’s 4.6 thanks to his 17 home runs at the plate and elite defense at second base for the Cardinals. Wetherholt’s glove was his calling card in 2026. His +25 outs above average , according to Statcast, were not only tops among MLB second basemen, but second only to MVP candidate Pete Crow-Armstrong’s 26 among all players, regardless of defensive position. The same goes for Wetherholt’s +23 fielding run value .
